choice.title: Graphics driver
choice.description: Metal on the host's GPU, through virtio-gpu and Venus: the kexts (one through OpenCore, two in the Auxiliary Kernel Collection), the Metal driver and the watcher that keeps it in place across macOS updates. Required. If OpenCore doesn't yet allow unsigned kexts (SIP 0x203) and AMFI's ad-hoc code (amfi_get_out_of_my_way=1), the installer sets them in OpenCore's config.plist, after backing it up.

choice.title: Hardware video
choice.description: Safari, QuickTime and every app that uses VideoToolbox decode H.264, HEVC and VP9 and encode H.264 and HEVC on the host's GPU. Adds VeneraVideo.kext through OpenCore. The host needs its half too: install-host.sh on the Proxmox host (Venera-host-@VERSION@.tar.gz). Without it, video decodes and encodes in software as before.

choice.title: Venera app
choice.description: A small app that runs at login: it tells you when something needs you (a macOS update took the driver off the system volume, the desktop fell back to software, the host's video service isn't running) and shows what runs. No menu bar icon unless you turn it on.

choice.title: Proxmox guest agent
choice.description: Lets Proxmox work with this VM as it does with Linux and Windows guests: Shutdown and Reboot from the Proxmox page shut macOS down cleanly, the VM's Summary shows its IP addresses, and the host can run commands and copy files in (qm guest exec, file-write), set an account's password (qm guest passwd) and set the clock. And the clipboard: copy and paste between the Proxmox console and macOS, both ways (text; images too with a SPICE client). Adds VeneraConsole.kext through OpenCore for the agent's port. Turn on QEMU Guest Agent in the VM's Options (VirtIO is fastest), and for the console's clipboard set the Display's Clipboard to VNC. It runs as root and answers only the Proxmox host, which already controls the VM. Takes the place of mac-guest-agent if that is installed.

choice.title: Safari WebGL (changes a security setting)
choice.description: Safari's graphics process only loads drivers from the system volume. This turns off SIP's authenticated root (csr 0x800, in OpenCore) and puts the Metal driver on the system volume, so WebGL in Safari uses the host's GPU. Every other app uses the GPU without it. If authenticated root is already off, the driver goes on the system volume whether or not this is chosen.
